marking: Multiple choice is checked against the supplied answer tables. Written questions use self-review with the original marking guide.
formatting: Chemical subscripts, superscripts, Symbol-font glyphs and MathML preserved; MCQ choices use formatted HTML.

notes: Guide heading lists 2,2,6 marks; the paper separates the 4-mark question 35 and 6-mark isomer question 36.
Supplied key B says sodium atom although the stem asks for a positively charged particle.
Paper allocates 3 marks to part (a), but the supplied guide allocates 2; total paper marks 7 retained.
Printed total is 8 marks; printed subparts total 10 marks.
Alternative question has no supplied answer; review draft key.
Printed total is 9 marks; printed subparts total 7 marks.
Alternative question has no supplied answer; review draft key.
No option is explicitly marked in the supplied key. Teacher must confirm the answer.
Supplied key selects D. Gallium-71 has 33 protons and 38 neutrons; Ga³⁺ has 30 electrons, giving B. Automatic marking is disabled.
Paper requests 4 significant figures; guide stem says 3 but its mark allocation says 4. The guide incorrectly prints a percent sign after relative atomic mass.
Supplied key selects D; the eight hydrogen atoms in (NH₄)₂SO₄ give option B. Automatic marking is disabled pending teacher review.
Source wording/equation requires review: the printed copper(I) oxide equation omits water.
Source wording/equation requires review: the prompt alternates between iron(III) oxide and iron(II) oxide.
Supplied key selects B. With a non-polar stationary phase, the least polar compound A is expected to have the longest retention. Teacher review is required.
Guide names a dichloro product although the source reaction uses bromine. Product should be 2,3-dibromobutane; supplied product boxes are blank.
Paper has 2 marks; guide includes extra naming rows. Only the matching structure and 2,3-dimethyloct-4-ene apply.
Paper labels the energy diagram 2 marks; guide says 3. Preserve the paper’s 12-mark total and review allocations.
The supplied Rutherford illustration includes Bohr-style electron shells; review or replace that illustration before use.
Instruction restates the self-contained table headings. Six other written questions are withheld because their prompts and givens are missing.
Supplied key selects D, but butane and 1-methylpropane denote the same structure. Option B (butanal and butanone) gives structural isomers. Teacher review is required.
Supplied key selects D. Equal volumes of the stated sulfuric acid and sodium hydroxide leave an acidic solution; confirm the indicator colours before marking.
Supplied key selects C. Option A describes the limitation of the Arrhenius definition to water. Teacher review is required.
The given +1 ion configuration has 26 electrons, whereas the supplied rubidium answer requires 36 electrons (2,8,18,8). Review the printed configuration.
Supplied key D conflicts with the liquid-mercury wording: liquid malleability (A) is also problematic. Review the stem and intended answer.
Supplied key selects A (3), which counts lone pairs on one chlorine atom. Cl₂ has 6 lone pairs in total, giving B. Automatic marking is disabled.
The list includes volume as a factor changing volume, apparently in place of temperature. Supplied key D is preserved; review the wording.
Supplied key C does not reflect ionisation of HCl in water. Option D describes covalent bonds broken and covalent/ion–dipole interactions formed. Teacher review is required.
Paper and guide use different energy-profile levels; read the values from the paper graph before marking.
Matching marking guide labels this question 9; paper labels it 8.
Paper header allocates 5 marks, but the calculation subpart prints 6 marks. Header allocation retained.
The guide’s methylbenzene side-chain chlorination requires UV light, which is not specified in the paper. Review reaction conditions.
The supplied 90 ppm answer conflicts with the plotted calibration line: peak area 12,000 corresponds to approximately 125–130 ppm. Review before marking.
Citric acid is triprotic; the paper describes it as monoprotic. Review this model simplification before use.
The stated −210°C is near nitrogen’s freezing point; ordinary liquid-nitrogen bath temperature is approximately −196°C. Review the supplied temperature.
Guide annotates half a mark per correct entry, which does not match the printed 3-mark total. Review the allocation; paper total retained.
Supplied key selects B (CₙH₂ₙ), but the general formula of an acyclic alkane is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, option D. Automatic marking is disabled.
Review the second handwritten alternative: the required isomer formula is C₄H₆Br₂.
Guide’s printed structure (c) differs from the paper; the handwritten correction matches the paper’s alkene. Use the paper’s structure.
Matching butane calculation is numbered 8 in the supplied key and 6 in the paper.
The source says isomers of copper; these are isotopes.

Supplied phosphine equation uses the incorrect product PO5. A balanced equation using empirical phosphorus pentoxide is 2PH₃ + 4O₂ → P₂O₅ + 3H₂O; using P₄O₁₀: 4PH₃ + 8O₂ → P₄O₁₀ + 6H₂O. Review before marking.

None of the listed sets contains only strong electrolytes: set I contains insoluble salts, II contains non-electrolytes and a weak acid, III contains weak ethanoic acid, and IV contains weak ammonia. Supplied key D retained for review; automatic marking disabled.

The premise of a dramatic conductivity decrease is questionable: hydroxide remains and sodium replaces precipitated barium in solution. Review the explanation rather than assuming all charge carriers are removed.
Part (a) gives volume of water rather than final solution volume. The supplied 1.516 mol L⁻¹ assumes final solution volume is 250 mL.
